data.narrative:
Revel, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Scott Morton, is evaluated against a universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ). The peer set includes same-stage companies: Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B), alongside later-stage private firms including Divergent and Exotec.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the company's $180M in total raised as a proxy base value, applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $342M. Peer-median methodology triangulates off three same-sector, same-stage comparables, producing a median valuation of $1.8B with a range of $1.6B to $2.0B. The peer-median approach carries greater weight given direct stage and sector alignment, whereas stage-progression relies on capital raised as a crude value proxy.

The triangulated analysis across both methods supports a valuation range of $291M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $1.0B. The wide spread reflects tension between the early-stage capital-based method and peer multiples for operationally mature Series B robotics firms. Key uncertainties include whether Revel's unit economics and commercialization progress align with the higher-valued peer set, and whether the 1.9x stage multiplier appropriately reflects category-specific risk and growth trajectories in manufacturing automation.
